hook_text: You cannot draw? Doesn't matter. The words on the sketch do the work. Here is how designers sketch two ideas and pick one.
clip_script: Two ideas, truly different: a paperboard take-away box and a returnable box with a deposit, not a big box and a small box. No ruler; pencil only, so the drawing keeps up with your brain. Faint box for proportions, firmer outline, tilt it so you see depth. Pull the parts apart to show how they fit. Slice it to show the rib inside. Then write everywhere: part names, material, sizes, and the forces, walls squashed when stacked, lid bends, fork stabs here. Now the table. Your rules down the side, two ideas across, tick, half-tick or cross with a reason. The returnable box cuts more waste, but the rank has no water to wash it. The paperboard box works today. Choose, write why, borrow the best bit from the loser, and keep both sketches.
visual_style: Pencil sketches a faint box, then a container, then a floating lid; labels and arrows pop in; a second sketch of a tagged returnable box appears; a table fills with ticks and one red cross at 'water'.
pacing: Two ideas, how to sketch, how to label, the table, the choice.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and sketch your team's two ideas with at least six labels each.
